speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To help diagnose your pruritic rash, could you describe the appearance of the lesions and tell me exactly when they started relative to your fever and respiratory symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: The facial rash sparing the perioral area is highly suggestive of "slapped cheek" syndrome. Can you describe the rash on her trunk and extremities, specifically if it appears lacy or reticular?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mildly pruritic rash on trunk and extremities. I also have Low-grade fever, Rhinorrhea, Headache, Facial rash not involving the perioral skin.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Does the rash on her trunk and extremities have a lacy or reticular pattern?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Social history: Attends local school. Lives with parents and one younger sibling. No recent travel history.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Given the classic "slapped cheek" rash followed by a lacy, reticular rash on the trunk and extremities, this presentation is pathognomonic for Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease).
DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease)
